synthesis.intent_alignment: DataForSEO's two intent signals disagree and are low-confidence: the dedicated search-intent endpoint labels the keyword 'navigational' at only 0.463 probability (near coin-flip), while the keyword-overview endpoint's bundled classification says 'commercial'. Read together with the SERP composition (a 3-result local pack, review-heavy organic listings, a Reddit cost-comparison thread, and a PAA question on cost), the likely searcher already knows they want ongoing/recurring cleaning and is now comparing named local providers on price and trust signals — closer to late-stage commercial comparison shopping than pure navigational lookup, but this reading should be treated as directional given the conflicting/low-confidence signals, not a confirmed classification.
competitor_takeaways: maidtoclean.com.au (organic rank 4, local pack #1, 4.8★/2,200 votes) states an exact hourly rate ('$71/hr') and a '200% Satisfaction Guarantee' up front, and builds trust through a named founder story and visible internal promos (referral bonus, Cleaner of the Month). Its pricing model is hourly, not membership-based — an opening for the client to reframe the pricing conversation around a flat, all-inclusive membership instead.

innercitymaids.com.au (organic rank 6, local pack #2, 5★/1,100 votes) wins on structural clarity: explicit 'no lock-in contract' messaging, a granular inclusions/exclusions task list per clean type, and a large suburb-tagged testimonial wall (St Kilda, Footscray, Fitzroy, and more). Its FAQ also states cleaning is 'usually carried out by one person' — a direct contrast point for the client's two-person dedicated team.

jimscleaning.com.au (organic rank 7, 4.8★/3,096 votes) leans on national franchise scale ('team of more than 800 specialist cleaning franchisees') and phone-first booking (131 546). The client's smaller, dedicated-team positioning is a legitimate differentiator against a franchise/volume model.

A Reddit r/melbourne thread ranks organically at position 5 for this exact keyword, with commenters discussing real prices paid ('around $300 for the entire house... 2-2.5 hours' for a 4 bed/3 bath). A forum thread outranking most competitor brand pages signals unmet demand for transparent, real-world cost discussion that brand pages currently avoid.

PAA data for this keyword is thin and partly off-topic: of the 4 questions returned, the 4th ('What is deep cleaning vs. regular cleaning?') resolved to an unrelated dental-cleaning site as its expanded source, not a house-cleaning competitor. The question topic itself is on-brief and worth answering, but the SERP's own suggested source should not be treated as a competitor content signal.
